en.t: It has been a long time since I took leave of your honored face.
My feeling of lonely desolation grows stronger with each passing day.
I am deeply grateful to have received your gracious letter.
The wording was extremely respectful and deferential.

units.source_text: 源氏展读此信，泪如雨下。

en.t: Genji unfolded and read the letter, and tears fell from him like rain.

units.source_text: 深恐旁人见了怀疑，勉强装作若无其事，然而愁绪填塞胸怀。

en.t: Afraid that others might see and grow suspicious, he forced himself to act as though nothing were wrong, yet sorrow filled his heart.

units.source_text: 他想起了从前尚侍胧月夜受朱雀院的弘徽殿母后监视时情状，与此事相似。

en.t: He remembered how Oborozukiyo, the former Naishi no Kami, had once been watched by Suzaku-in's mother of Kokiden, and how similar that situation had been to this one.

units.source_text: 但此事恐是近在目前之故，似觉更加痛苦，世间少有其类。

en.t: But perhaps because this matter was so immediately before him, it seemed even more painful, almost without equal in the world.

units.source_text: 他想：“好色之人，真是自寻烦恼。

en.t: He thought, Lovers truly bring trouble upon themselves.

units.source_text: 从今以后，我不再做烦心之事了。

en.t: From now on, I will no longer do things that distress my heart.

units.source_text: 况且这种恋情本是不应有的。”

en.t: Besides, this kind of love should never have existed in the first place.

units.source_text: 努力自制，十分痛苦，便取琴来弹，忽又想起玉鬘抚弦的纤指。

en.t: Struggling painfully to restrain himself, he took up the koto to play, but suddenly remembered Tamakazura's slender fingers touching the strings.

units.source_text: 他就在和琴上作清弹，吟唱“蕴藻不可连根采”之歌。

en.t: He played clear notes on the wagon and sang the song, The waterweed must not be plucked up by the roots.

units.source_text: 其神态之优美，若教所恋之人见了，怕不得不动心吧。

en.t: His bearing was so graceful that, if the woman he loved had seen him, she could hardly have helped being moved.

units.source_text: 冷泉帝自从一见玉鬘芳容之后，心中念念不忘。

en.t: Ever since Emperor Reizei had once seen Tamakazura's lovely face, he had been unable to forget her.

units.source_text: “银红衫子窈窕姿”那首俚俗的古歌，成了他的口头禅，使他终日悬念。

en.t: That vulgar old song about a graceful figure in a pale crimson robe became a phrase always on his lips and kept him longing for her all day.

units.source_text: 他好几次偷偷地写信给玉鬘。

en.t: Several times he secretly wrote letters to Tamakazura.

units.source_text: 玉鬘自伤命薄，对于酬酢赠答之事，亦觉无甚意味，因此并未写过真心诚意的回信。

en.t: Tamakazura lamented her own unlucky fate and found little meaning in such exchanges of gifts and replies, so she never wrote him a truly heartfelt answer.

units.source_text: 她始终记念源氏太政大臣对她的恩惠，觉得甚可感谢，永远不能忘记。

en.t: She always remembered the kindness that Genji, the Grand Minister, had shown her, felt deeply grateful for it, and could never forget it.
